judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-3.2 ('Describes location and movement using common and mathematical language; understands the concept of a map') within CG-3's spatial-relationships goal. The Class-3 content (rank 2) has learners describe position and location in a simple, familiar route map (home to school) using everyday spatial language; the Class-4 content (rank 3) requires describing the location of objects in a grid, a more formalised, structured reference frame (LC tags add 'grid' and 'spatial' to the shared 'location'/'position'). Facility with informally describing position/location in a route map plausibly supports success in the more abstract grid-referenced location task, so the lower-to-higher direction first_to_second is developmentally supported rather than mere same-topic repetition. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the two ancestors lack developmental coordinates, so the judgment rests on the bounded description, coordinate ranks, and LC text supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-4.2 (selecting and using suitable units and tools for measuring attributes) and Curricular Goal CG-4. The second SFI (Class-3, rank 2) specifies concrete measurement of length in metre, half metre, quarter metre and more/less than 1 metre using a measuring tape, with LCs on measuring and comparing lengths with a standard tool. The first SFI (Class-4, rank 3) generalises to the estimate-measure-verify cycle, with LCs 'Estimate the measure of attributes of objects', 'Measure an attribute of an object using suitable units' and 'Verify a measured value against the estimate'. Competent hands-on measuring with standard length units and a tool supports the later, more demanding estimation-then-verification work applied to attributes generally, so the lower-rank Class-3 content builds towards the Class-4 content (second_to_first, the only permitted developmental direction). judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under CG-1 but sit in different competencies: the Class-2 item (C-1.11, 'Addition and subtraction problems involving money up to ₹99', LCs: solve addition/subtraction money problems) is an applied money-transaction computation, while the Class-1 item (C-1.8, 'Estimates the sum and difference of numbers', LCs: estimate the sum / estimate the difference of numbers) is an estimation/number-sense strategy, not exact computation. judgment.rationale: Both are Class-1 Content (rank 0, same rank) under CG-1 but different competencies: the second is counting ('Counts objects up to 20 both forward and backward', C-1.6, LCs 'count objects up to 20 forward/backward'), the first is early data handling ('Collects, represents and interprets simple data ... draws conclusions as more than / less than / equal to', C-1.12, LCs 'collect simple data by observing visuals', 'represent simple data', 'interpret simple data to draw conclusions as more than, less than or equal to'). The first explicitly requires quantifying and comparing sets of objects observed in a picture (e.g. flowers in a garden) to judge more than/less than/equal to, which rests on secure enumeration of small object sets; so proficiency in counting objects up to 20 substantively supports success in collecting and interpreting simple picture data. Same-rank direction is grounded in this specific quantification-to-comparison dependency, not in the shared CG-1 ancestor, shared stopword tokens ('and', 'to') or adjacent source pages, which carry no semantic weight.
